notes: Version ranges are taken from the linked advisories, not from video transcripts. 'confidence' is 'confirmed' when NVD or the vendor gives the fixed release, 'reported' when only third-party write-ups do. A vulnerability applies when introduced <= installed < fixed. A null 'fixed' means no fixed release is known.

vulnerabilities.name: Bleeding Llama
vulnerabilities.summary: Ollama's GGUF loader trusts declared tensor sizes. A crafted GGUF pushed through /api/create and /api/push returns a slice of the server's heap memory: environment variables, API keys, system prompts and other users' conversations.
vulnerabilities.remediation: Update Ollama to 0.17.1 or later, and keep it bound to 127.0.0.1.

vulnerabilities.name: Unsigned Windows auto-update
vulnerabilities.summary: Ollama for Windows does not verify the signature of downloaded updates (the verification routine always succeeds) and installs them silently. Chained with CVE-2026-42249 this gives persistent code execution.
vulnerabilities.remediation: Update Ollama, and until you have confirmed your version includes the fix, turn off automatic updates.

vulnerabilities.name: Windows updater path traversal
vulnerabilities.summary: The Ollama for Windows updater builds the staged installer path from HTTP response headers without sanitising them, letting an attacker plant a file that runs at every login.
vulnerabilities.remediation: Update Ollama, and until you have confirmed your version includes the fix, turn off automatic updates.

vulnerabilities.name: Desktop app drive-by (no CVE assigned)
vulnerabilities.summary: Any web page could silently point the Ollama desktop app's 'Remote' setting at an attacker server, which then sees your chats. The malicious setting persists after updating.
vulnerabilities.remediation: Update Ollama, then check the desktop app's connection settings for an unexpected remote server.

vulnerabilities.name: Probllama (digest path traversal)
vulnerabilities.summary: Ollama did not validate model digests, so pulling a model from a malicious registry could write files anywhere and lead to remote code execution.

vulnerabilities.name: DNS rebinding
vulnerabilities.summary: A malicious web page could use DNS rebinding to reach the local Ollama API from your browser.

vulnerabilities.name: Llama Drama
vulnerabilities.summary: llama-cpp-python rendered GGUF chat templates with an unsandboxed Jinja environment, so a malicious template runs arbitrary code on every prompt.

vulnerabilities.name: SGLang chat template SSTI
vulnerabilities.summary: SGLang rendered model-supplied chat templates with a plain jinja2.Environment, so a poisoned GGUF gives remote code execution (reached through /v1/rerank).
vulnerabilities.remediation: Upgrade SGLang to 0.5.11 or later, and do not serve untrusted GGUF files.
